solves.reasoning: ② 'defining' is wrong. 'even the objects that haven't been defining yet' — the verb 'define' is used in passive voice (objects are defined), so it requires past participle 'defined', not present participle 'defining'. Correct: 'haven't been defined'.
④ 'similar' is wrong. 'We reason similar in everyday life' — 'similar' is an adjective but 'reason' is a verb, so an adverb is needed to modify it. Correct: 'similarly' (adverb form).

③ 'knowing' is wrong. 'belongs to a class already knowing to have this property' — the class doesn't actively know; it is passively known to others. The correct form is past participle 'known' (as in 'is known to'), not 'knowing'.

③ 'what' is wrong. 'this guarantees what every object within a class has a particular property' — 'guarantees' takes a noun clause introduced by 'that', not 'what'. 'What' creates a nominal clause meaning 'the thing that', which doesn't work here. Correct: 'guarantees that'.

④ 'serve' is wrong. 'Mathematical calculation ability serve as a key indicator' — the subject 'Mathematical calculation ability' is singular, so the verb must be singular: 'serves', not 'serve' (plural).

③ 'reject' is wrong. 'belongs to a class already known to reject this property' — the point of the proof strategy is to find a class that has (possesses) the property. Reject means to not have it, which is the opposite. Passage says 'have this property'.

③ 'eliminated' is wrong. 'even the objects that haven't been eliminated yet' — the passage talks about objects that haven't been defined yet (not yet formally established). Eliminated means removed/deleted, which contradicts the mathematical context of objects awaiting formal definition.

④ 'differently' is wrong. 'We reason differently in everyday life' — the passage establishes a parallel between mathematical reasoning and everyday reasoning, saying we do this 'similarly' (not differently). 'Differently' contradicts the comparison being made.
② 'wastes' is wrong. 'This wastes huge amounts of time and effort' — the passage says clustering objects together SAVES time and effort (not wastes it). Wastes is the direct opposite of saves.
